title: The Pomace and the Prize
introduction: Cider-making round here is less an industry than a feud conducted in barns. Every maker will tell you, unprompted, that the neighbours' barrels smell of a pickled sock. Judging day brings a small silver cup and several long-standing grudges. Pomace, for the uninitiated, is the pulpy mash of crushed apples left in the press once the juice has run out.
preamble:
Five makers are involved. Determine each maker's pressing month and fault.
- **Maker**: Jethro, Araminta, Haskell, Morwenna and Petroc.
- **Pressing month** (listed from earlier to later): January, February, March, April and May.
- **Fault**: a stuck ferment, mousiness, sulphur, acetification and ropiness.
Every maker has a different pressing month and fault, so within each category every item is used exactly once.
clues: The maker accused of mousiness presses in May, and the maker accused of ropiness presses in the month immediately before May.
The maker accused of acetification presses in the month immediately before February.
Araminta presses in the month immediately after March.
Jethro presses in the month immediately before the maker accused of a stuck ferment, who in turn presses earlier than Petroc.
